segmentation.text: Except if required by an emergency
or as otherwise authorized by subsection 3
a person shall not drive a vehicle
Across any solid white line that separates an entrance or exit lane from a marked traffic lane.
A person driving a vehicle described in
paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210
may drive that vehicle on a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.
The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to:
(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;
(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;
or (f) A public transit motor bus,
that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: An emergency requiring the movement is not observable; it is read through the conduct that shows it: the subject's hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard, "both indicators flashing together"), or the subject an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency") showing a lit warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp, "a warning lamp lit"). ru.emergency_vehicle is "not a stand-in for a responding emergency vehicle — the class alone is not responding": the class is read only together with its lit warning lamp.

Authorization by subsection 3 is the permission subsection 3 states (spans e7, e10, e12-e18): a shoulder-use permission posted by a dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", of code shoulder_use_permitted; this span joins that permission to the duty as an exception.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway". "drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle is moving, drv.motion.complete_halt not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060, "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only"): st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes", whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies).

Driving across the line between two lanes is the subject's footprint first reaching from lane r1 into the neighbouring lane r2 on side s: drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane, "Road user a, occupying lane r1, begins to move into lane r2, the neighbouring lane of the same direction on side s of r1". The line crossed is the marking on side s of r1: st.lane_marking, "per side of a lane: type ... colour", of type solid or double_solid and colour white. It separates an entrance or exit lane from a marked traffic lane where, of r1 and r2 (st.lane), one is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance or exit and the other is governed by no such sign. The regulatory sign is "not a stand-in for a road feature": the lane's role is read from the sign that indicates it, as subsection 1 reads entrances and exits.
The person driving a vehicle of the classes listed (e12-e17): the subject vehicle, admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; which vehicles are described is read from the list.

On a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder while it occupies the st.controlled_access region; the signage allowing that vehicle to use the shoulder is a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governing that shoulder (dev.governs), whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold, "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user").

"Authorized emergency vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law"; the words borrowed through the reference e8 list it as "(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;". The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;": a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws". The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service", kind incident_management; not an emergency vehicle. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(d) A tow car;": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, "a motor vehicle which has been altered or designed and equipped for and exclusively used in the business of towing vehicles". The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(e) A coroner vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service", kind coroner; not an emergency vehicle. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"or (f) A public transit motor bus,": a member of DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus ("a vehicle ... designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation") that is ru.transit_bus, "bus in public transit service". The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

Being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway: the listed vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder lying on (st.on_way) the st.highway it is on, governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted whose conditions hold for it (prim.conditions_hold). The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

compositions.quote: (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;
compositions.why: The reference borrows only the list of vehicle classes NRS 484B.210(4) sets forth (an authorized emergency vehicle, one under permit as such, a traffic incident management vehicle, a tow car, a coroner vehicle, a public transit motor bus) to name which vehicles subsection 3 permits on a signed paved shoulder; no rule of NRS 484B.210 (its passing on the right, or its exemption from it) needs to apply, hold or be complied with for this duty or its exception, and the list's words are appended in this line and carried by its own elements.

residues.why: Introduces the list of NRS 484B.210(4) as appended; the exemption from the passing rule of NRS 484B.210(1)(c)(1) it states is that section's, not this duty's, and is not read here.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle in motion (drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold) whose footprint overlaps a controlled-access highway ca (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access). Exceptions: the duty does not apply where the subject's hazard lamps flash (sig.hazard) or it is an emergency vehicle with a lit warning lamp (ru.emergency_vehicle, sig.warning_lamp); nor where the subject, a listed vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, ru.official_vehicle of kind incident_management or coroner, DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, or DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus with ru.transit_bus), occupies a paved shoulder on the highway it is on that a shoulder_use_permitted dev.regulatory_sign governs with its conditions holding for it.
obligation: At no such observation does drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane(subject, r1, r2, s) hold, for lanes r1 and r2 and a side s in {left, right}, where the st.lane_marking on side s of r1 is of type solid or double_solid and colour white, and of r1 and r2 one is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance or exit and the other by no such sign.

narrowings.why: "a person shall not drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle in motion is driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
An emergency is read through the conduct that shows it: hazard lamps flashing, or an emergency vehicle showing a lit warning lamp.
An entrance or exit lane is read as a lane an entrance- or exit-coded regulatory sign governs, and a marked traffic lane as a mapped lane no such sign governs.

Driving across the line is read at the observation the footprint first reaches over it into the neighbouring lane; a solid_broken marking, whose solid side cannot be told from the per-side record, is not read as a solid line.
"lawfully placed" signage is read from the presence of a shoulder_use_permitted sign governing the shoulder.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a controlled-access highway, the subject car in an entrance lane (governed by an entrance-coded sign) moves at 22 m/s and its footprint first reaches into the adjacent through lane across a solid white marking on that side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car in the entrance lane merges into the through lane where the marking between them on that side is broken white.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car changes lanes across a solid white line on a surface street; it never overlaps a controlled-access region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves from the entrance lane into the through lane on a controlled-access highway; the source does not observe lane markings.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An emergency vehicle with lit warning lamps crosses the solid white line from the through lane into an exit lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject car crosses a solid white line between two through lanes, neither governed by an entrance or exit sign.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of vehicle tracking sources
